subject: Burst policy automation + telemetry hookup for Synapse Labs Dedicated pools
messages:
From: Ari Mehta <ari.mehta@synapselabs.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-21T16:12:00Z
Subject: Dedicated capacity: projected burst windows and telemetry hookup

Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Synapse is close to finalizing estimates for our dedicated deployment, but before procurement we need to lock down how burst capacity will be handled operationally. A few specific asks: 

- Can Redwood automate temporary slab increases during our nightly peak (00:00–03:00 PDT) for the first 30 days of a release?
- We need a telemetry stream that exports per-request latency and queue-depth metrics (1-min granularity) into our Datadog account for 90 days.
- What are the eviction guarantees if we hit 95% GPU utilization across the slab?

I've attached a forecast spreadsheet with hourly peak estimates for the next 3 months. Procurement cc'd.

Thanks,
Ari Mehta
Head of Platform
Synapse Labs

Attachments: synapse_burst_forecast_v3.xlsx (excel/spreadsheet, 128KB)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Mehta <ari.mehta@synapselabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-22T00:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: projected burst windows and telemetry hookup

Ari —

Appreciate the clarity in the forecast. Quick answers up front, then I’ll loop in engineering to nail the implementation details: 

- Automated temporary slab increases: yes — we can provision a scheduled "shoulder burst" policy scoped to the first 30 days post-release. We recommend a maximum uplift of 40% for safety (we can be more conservative depending on your forecast).
- Telemetry: we can stream the per-request metrics to your Datadog via an integration key. Retention for streaming is configurable; we can keep 90 days on the platform side and forward everything to your account.
- Eviction at 95%: our policy is graceful throttle with prioritized preemption. Ephemeral non-reserved workloads will be evicted first; reserved instances in the dedicated slab remain pinned per contract. We can encode stricter eviction windows as a policy.

I’m looping in Kimberly (SE) to propose a concrete autoscale policy and Ben from runtime to validate feasibility for the peak patterns you sent.

Next steps: Kimberly will propose a playbook and a short runbook we can put into the addendum. If that sounds good we’ll get a first draft of the service addendum to procurement.

Best,
Sergio
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Mehta <ari.mehta@synapselabs.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-22T10:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: projected burst windows and telemetry hookup

Ari —

Thanks for the forecast. I pulled the spreadsheet and sketched a candidate autoscale policy that maps to your hourly peaks. High level summary below, full playbook attached: 

- Policy name: synapse-night-shoulder-30d
- Trigger: schedule + predictive threshold (if forecasted 60-min rolling avg > 70% for 3 consecutive windows)
- Action: provision up to +40% dedicated slab for a max of 6 hours per calendar day during the 00:00–06:00 PDT window
- Cooldown: 20 minutes after the last 5-min average falls below 60%
- Fall back: if cluster remains >90% for 15 minutes, redirect new requests to a lower-cost compatible model variant (opt-0.9) and notify Synapse via webhook

Telemetry hookup: we will stream the following to your Datadog API key: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), model load, queue depth, and eviction events. Frequency: 1-min metrics, 30s events for eviction/scale actions.

I’ve attached a draft runbook with play-level ops and an example Datadog dashboard. If you’re comfortable with +40% cap I can convert this into addendum language and share for procurement.

-Kim
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: synapse-night-playbook.pdf (pdf, 210KB); redwood-dedicated-service-addendum-draft_v1.pdf (pdf, 45KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Ari Mehta <ari.mehta@synapselabs.com>
Date: 2028-09-23T02:17:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: projected burst windows and telemetry hookup

Ari/Kim —

Quick tech notes from runtime: the forecast shows several contiguous multi-hour spikes on Thursdays between 01:00–04:00 UTC (which is your PDT midnight window). Our concerns and suggestions: 

- Warm-up: to avoid cold-start tail latency, we recommend pre-warming up to 60% of the uplift 10 minutes before the scheduled window based on the schedule or a predictive signal from your forecast.
- KV cache priming: if you use long-context models we can prime KV caches from recent traffic; we need a small sample corpus (I flagged the forecast doc for a column).
- Eviction semantics: at sustained 95% we will first drain low-priority worker slots and move batchable requests into the batch queue. If pressure continues we will preempt ephemeral spot workloads. Reserved model pins remain intact.
- Safetyband: implement a soft-fail fallback route to opt-0.9 (as Kim suggested) and configure an automatic rollback if SLO degradation exceeds 8% p95.

Operational ask: give us write access to the forecast doc & a Datadog API key (scoped ingest-only). We’ll provision a staging policy into your sandbox and run two simulated bursts before the production cutover.

—Ben
Senior Runtime Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Ari Mehta <ari.mehta@synapselabs.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@synapselabs.com
Date: 2028-09-25T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: projected burst windows and telemetry hookup

Team —

This looks sensible. Procurement is asking for two items before we sign: 

1) A clear definition in the SAA (service addendum) of what constitutes an "authorized burst" vs. an "emergency surge" and the billing treatment for each.
2) A 30-day SLA for telemetry delivery uptime (we need assurances the Datadog forwarder will not drop metrics during scale events).

We are comfortable with the +40% uplift and pre-warm plan provided Ben can run the two simulated bursts in the staging cluster next week. I will share a scoped Datadog ingest key and grant edit on the forecast.

Thanks,
Ari
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Mehta <ari.mehta@synapselabs.com>, procurement@synapselabs.com
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-28T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: projected burst windows and telemetry hookup

Ari / Synapse procurement team —

Thanks for the clear asks. We will: 

- Add explicit definitions to the SAA: 
  * "Authorized Burst": scheduled or forecast-driven uplift agreed in advance (e.g., synapse-night-shoulder-30d) and billed at standard dedicated uplift rates in the contract appendix.
  * "Emergency Surge": unplanned rapid increases triggered by anomalies; subject to overage billing at a premium rate and manual approval for sustained >2 hour windows.

- Telemetry SLA: we will include a 30-day forwarder availability SLO (99.9% monthly) and a mitigation clause that includes replay windows for missed metrics for up to 48 hours.

Action items: 
- Ben to run the two staging simulations w/ Datadog key (ETA: 2028-09-30).
- Kim to convert playbook into redline language in the addendum (ETA: 2028-10-02).
- Sergio to send the first addendum draft to procurement once redlines are in.

I'll move these into the HubSpot deal and attach the addendum draft. Please confirm and we can target a signature the week of Oct 9.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Commercial Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-dedicated-service-addendum-draft_v1.pdf
